meta.premise: Long ago the sky broke and the Storm came down. It never fully left. Aethyr is a continent of proud survivor-cultures raised in the ruin of a vanished golden age, where weather is a living force, old empires lie buried under ash and ice, and every people tells a different story about who broke the sky.
meta.worldRule: Kin is broad heritage; Lineage is a specific ancestry, region, environment, magical influence, or cultural branch. No Kin or Lineage locks a character into any Class or Discipline.

regions.name: The Crownlands
regions.climate: Temperate river valleys, long autumns, mild wet winters
regions.description: The green heart of Aethyr, a patchwork of river-duchies, walled market-cities and old battlefields turned farmland. The Crownlands were the seat of the Old Empire that fell in the Great Sundering, and every plough here eventually turns up imperial coin, bone, or worse. It is the most multicultural region of the world: its free cities keep no single Kin as master.
resources: Grain, wine, river-iron, imperial salvage, guild banking
conflicts: Duchies quarrel over the vacant imperial throne
Salvage-rights wars over buried Old Empire vaults
Guilds versus nobility over city charters
landmarks: The Sundered Throne (a shattered imperial seat no one may sit in)
The Nine Bridges of Ninebridge Hold
The Drowned Palace beneath Bridgewater
hooks: A duke hires outsiders to open an imperial vault before a rival does
A dead emperor's crown surfaces in a river and three cities want it
The Sundered Throne begins to whisper again

regions.name: The Stormreach
regions.climate: Permanent storm-belt: chained thunderheads, standing lightning, wind that never sleeps
regions.description: A coastal expanse where the Storm that broke the sky still lives, wandering the land as walking tempests. People here do not shelter from weather so much as bargain with it. Stormreach folk read the sky like scripture and raise their halls on ridgelines to court the lightning rather than hide from it.
resources: Storm-glass, charged crystal, sky-iron, weather augury
conflicts: Rival storm-cults claim to speak for the living Storm
Coastal holds war over the few calm harbors
Debate on whether the Storm should be worshipped, fought, or freed
landmarks: The Standing Bolt (a lightning strike frozen mid-air for a century)
Skybell Reach, whose bronze bells never stop ringing in the wind
The Eye, a permanent hole of calm at the storm's center
hooks: The Storm speaks a name and it is your character's
A hold's Storm Bell has fallen silent for the first time in memory
Someone claims to have walked into the Eye and come back changed

regions.name: The Ironspine Mountains
regions.climate: Alpine and subterranean, bitter peaks over warm forge-deep halls
regions.description: The stone backbone of the continent: a titanic range riddled with dwarven forge-cities, goliath high-holds, and the tunnels of the Deep folk. The Ironspine is where the world keeps its metal and its grudges. Above the cloud line, sky-clans cross ancient bridges; below, forge-fires have burned without pause since before the Sundering.
resources: Iron, sky-iron, gemstone, rune-coal, master smithing
conflicts: Forge-cities feud over ore-veins and forgotten vault claims
Deep folk and surface dwarves disagree on how far down is too far
High-clans and forgemoot argue over who owns the peaks versus the roots
landmarks: The Everforge of Durnhal
The Nine Bridges above the cloud line
The Sealed Door of Emberdeep, which no one has opened and lived
hooks: A forge-city's Everforge is dimming and no one knows why
A vault claim erupts into clan war
Something is knocking on the Sealed Door from the inside

regions.name: The Emerald Wilds
regions.climate: Vast temperate-to-tropical old-growth forest, misted and green year round
regions.description: An immense living forest older than any kingdom, where elven realms, beast-kin ranges, and hidden groves overlap under one canopy. The Wilds are not empty wilderness but a contested green nation of many peoples who share the trees and rarely the rules. Cutting the wrong tree can start a war.
creatures: The Hunt (a spectral pack that rides the deep wood)
resources: Hardwood, herbcraft, living-wood bows, rare game, druidic reagents
conflicts: Elven high-realms versus wandering beast-kin ranges over hunting grounds
The Thorn Court's isolationism versus the Canopy Pact's open borders
Loggers and frontier settlers pressing the tree line
landmarks: The Heartwood, a tree said to remember the whole forest
The Silent Glade where sound will not travel
Elarethil, a city grown, not built
hooks: The Heartwood is sickening and blames outsiders
The Hunt has begun riding by day
A grove-treaty is broken and both sides want a neutral witness

regions.name: The Ashen Wastes
regions.climate: Grey volcanic desert, ashfall, ember-storms, sudden lava
regions.description: Where an empire burned. The Ashen Wastes are the scorched grave of a lost civilization and the ember-fires never fully died. Orc ash-clans, ember-touched dragonborn, and scavenger goblins live off what the fire left, walking the ash between glass ruins and cinder-cones.
conflicts: Ash-clans raid one another over water and glass ruins
Pilgrims who believe the fire is holy versus those who want it out
Everyone versus what still walks the burned capital
landmarks: The Glass Capital, a city fused to obsidian in a single night
The Everburn, a fire that has never gone out
The Ashfall Road paved with the bones of an army
hooks: A map to an unburned vault in the Glass Capital
The Everburn is spreading
An ash-clan elder claims the fire is finally ready to speak

regions.name: The Frostbound North
regions.climate: Subarctic to arctic: fjords, glaciers, white winters, brief fierce summers
regions.description: A hard white country of fjords, ice-plains, and glacier-halls. The North breeds endurance and long memory. Northlander humans, frost-touched orcs and goliaths, and polar beast-kin share a land where the aurora is read as an ancestor-fire and the cold is treated as a living, judging thing.
resources: Furs, whale-ivory, glacier-glass, amber, hardy longships
conflicts: Ice-reaver raiders versus settled fjord-holds
Aurora-keepers and frost-moot argue over ancestor rites
Southern colonists pressing north for glacier-glass
landmarks: The Aurora Vault, where the North keeps its dead kings under ice
The Frozen Fleet locked in a harbor of ice
The Long Bridge of glacier stone across a frozen fjord
hooks: A dead king is thawing out of the Aurora Vault
The Winter Hunt has crossed south of its old bounds
The Frozen Fleet's ice is cracking

regions.name: The Sunscorch Desert
regions.climate: Hot sand-sea and rock desert, killing days, cold star-bright nights
regions.description: A golden sea of dunes and buried cities under a merciless sun. The Sunscorch hides more history than any region, swallowed and preserved by the sand. Desert humans, lionkin prides, sun-elf caravans, and genasi flame-folk trade along oasis-roads and guard the secret of where the old cities sleep.
resources: Spice, salt, glass, sun-gold, buried antiquities
conflicts: Caravan-league versus sun-court over oasis tariffs
Grave-robbers versus sand-readers who keep the buried cities sealed
Prides and city-folk over water rights
landmarks: Sunspire, a mile-high needle that casts no shadow at noon
The Buried City of Karan-That-Was
The Mirror Flats where the sky reflects underfoot
hooks: A sandstorm has uncovered a city that should have stayed buried
The sun-court's heir is lost in the deep dunes
Someone is selling maps to the Buried City and the sand-readers want them dead

regions.name: The Moonlit Vale
regions.climate: Cool misted highland valley in perpetual dusk and moonlight
regions.description: A haunting valley where it is always evening. The Moon hangs low and the light never fully fades to dark or brightens to day. Kitsune tricksters, moon-elves, owlkin seers, and quiet human villages live by lunar tides and dream-omens. Nothing here is quite what it seems, and the Vale likes it that way.
conflicts: Moon-court intrigue where duels are fought with secrets
Dream-wardens versus those who traffic in stolen dreams
The border where the Vale bleeds into the Shadowlands
landmarks: Silvermere, a lake that shows not your face but your fate
The Hall of Nine Lanterns that must never all go dark
The Turning Wood where paths rearrange by moonlight
hooks: One of the Nine Lanterns has gone out
A face in Silvermere is your own, older and afraid
A kitsune noble owes you a favor and that is more dangerous than a debt

regions.name: The Blackdeep
regions.climate: Lightless subterranean world, warm near magma, cold in the far tunnels
regions.description: The underworld beneath the Ironspine and beyond: a whole hidden civilization of lightless kingdoms, fungal forests, and cavern-seas. The Deep dwarves, drow, cave goblins, and things older than either raise cities by the glow of stone. Down here, a lantern is a target and silence is a language.
resources: Deep-crystal, glowcap, black-iron, blind-pearl, forbidden lore
conflicts: Drow houses' endless succession wars
Deep-conclave versus surface expeditions
Who owns the Sunless Market and its neutral peace
landmarks: The Sunless Market, the one place all Deep peoples keep the peace
The Glowfall, an underground waterfall of luminous stone
The Deepest Door, below which the Deep folk refuse to dig
hooks: Something is coming up through the Deepest Door
A drow house hires surface blades for a war its own kind won't fight
The Glowfall is going dark, tunnel by tunnel

regions.name: The Sapphire Sea
regions.climate: Warm bright ocean, trade winds, reef-shallows and open blue
regions.description: The great bright ocean and its thousand islands, ruled by no crown and crossed by every flag. Seaborn tide-folk, turtlekin island-elders, coastal humans, and birdkin sailors make the Sapphire Sea the world's marketplace and its most contested water. Above the waves it is trade; below, it is another world entirely.
resources: Pearl, coral, salt, fish, trade goods, shipwreck salvage
conflicts: Free-captains versus the tide-covenant's toll-lines
Surface trade versus seaborn undersea claims
Reef territory wars between island turtlekin elders
landmarks: Port Meridian, the neutral crossroads of all sea-trade
The Coral Throne of the tide-covenant
The Graveyard Reef where sunk fleets rest
hooks: A free-captain needs a crew to raid a covenant toll-vault
The Graveyard Reef has surfaced a ship that sank a hundred years ago
Something in the deep is driving the reef-serpents ashore

regions.name: The Abyssal Trench
regions.climate: Crushing lightless deep-ocean, cold, pressure, bioluminescent dark
regions.description: The bottom of the world's ocean, a trench so deep the sun is a rumor. Abyss-born seaborn and things without names keep court in the crushing dark around vents of black fire. Few surface folk go down and fewer return, and those that do speak of a drowned city that was never built by human hands.
resources: Black-fire pearl, abyss-glass, deep-song, drowned relics
conflicts: Abyss-choir cults versus surface seaborn who fear them
Vent-wardens guarding what sleeps near the black fire
Salvagers versus the crushing dark itself
landmarks: The Drowned Spire, a tower rising from the trench floor
The Black Fire vents
The Silent Deep where even bioluminescence dies
hooks: The Drowned Spire has lit up for the first time in an age
An abyss-choir hymn is being heard in surface harbors
Something the size of an island is moving up the trench

regions.name: The Skyward Isles
regions.climate: High-altitude floating islands, thin cold air, endless sky and cloud-seas
regions.description: Broken chunks of an ancient land that never fell, held aloft by old sky-magic and the living Storm. The Skyward Isles drift above the world, home to seraphim high-realms, birdkin aeries, harengon sky-clans, and the daring who cross between islands on gliders and bridges of chain and cloud. To be grounded here is to be lost.
conflicts: Aerie-clans versus sky-covenant over island claims
Isles that are slowly sinking and who gets the lifeboats
Ground-born refugees seeking asylum aloft
landmarks: Cloudspire, the highest inhabited point in the world
The Chain Bridges strung between drifting isles
The Sinking Isle, dropping a hand-span each year
hooks: An isle has begun to fall and thousands live on it
A Chain Bridge is cut and someone profits
The sky-covenant seeks proof of what holds the isles up before it fails

regions.name: The Celestial Heights
regions.climate: Rarefied luminous upper heaven, starlight, aurora, unearthly stillness
regions.description: The highest realm mortals can reach, a place of star-fire and impossible light where the seraphim keep their oldest halls and the sky is close enough to touch. The Heights are less a country than a threshold, half in the world and half out of it. Time runs strangely here and few who climb come down unchanged.
creatures: The Fallen (seraphim who chose the ground)
resources: Starlight-glass, radiant ore, celestial song, prophecy
conflicts: Radiant-choir orthodoxy versus the fallen-covenant's heresy
Whether mortals should be allowed to climb at all
A schism over a prophecy of the sky breaking again
landmarks: The Star Court, where the constellations are said to hold council
The Threshold, edge of the world and the beyond
Dawnhold, first light every morning
hooks: A prophecy names your character in the Star Court's records
A Fallen seraph asks you to carry a message the choir has forbidden
The stars over the Threshold have begun to go out

regions.name: The Shadowlands
regions.climate: Twilight umbral country, no true day, cold mist, long shadows with minds
regions.description: A dim border-country where the light of the world thins and the dark grows teeth. The Shadowlands are shunned and inhabited both: shadow-touched lineages, exiled vampires, night-hunters, and refugees who had nowhere brighter to go. It is not evil so much as unlit, and things that hate the sun have long memories here.
conflicts: Night-court vampire politics versus the living who share their dusk
Shadow-wardens holding the border against what is deeper in
The Unlit cult that wants to put out the sun for good
landmarks: Gloamhold, a fortress-city that has never seen dawn
The Threshold of Long Shadows
The Grey Market where the living and the returned trade as equals
hooks: The border-light is failing and the dark is advancing
A night-court noble seeks a living envoy no one will miss
The Unlit have found something that can dim a sun

regions.name: The Elemental Marches
regions.climate: Reality-thin borderland where fire, water, stone, storm and wind realms bleed through
regions.description: The frontier where the raw elemental realms press against the world and the two leak into each other. Rivers of flame, floating stone, standing storms, and pools of living water share one impossible country. Genasi elemental-folk, storm-touched dragonborn, and stone-goliaths guard the Marches, keeping the elements from spilling further inland.
resources: Pure elemental essence, rift-crystal, primal reagents, tempered alloys
conflicts: Marchwardens versus elemental-pacts over how much to bargain with the realms
Rifts widening and who caused them
Cults seeking to open a rift entirely
landmarks: Fourwinds, where four elemental realms meet at one crossroads
The Standing Rift, a permanent tear into the storm-realm
The Tempered Gate, forged to hold an elemental tide
hooks: A rift is widening and the Tempered Gate is failing
An elemental-pact has offered your character power for a terrible price
Something walked out of the Standing Rift wearing a person's shape

history.summary: The world before the sky broke. Almost nothing survives but ruins, legends, and the buried cities the sand and ice keep. Every culture claims descent from it and none can prove it.
events: The raising of the first cities by hands no living Kin remembers
The making of the sky-magic that still holds the Skyward Isles aloft
The first bargains with the elemental realms

history.summary: The Old Empire rose in the Crownlands and spread across most of Aethyr, uniting many Kin under one throne. Its roads, coins, and vaults are still everywhere underfoot.
events: The founding of the Old Empire and the Sundered Throne
The Concord of Kin that first bound many peoples under one law
The imperial vaults sealed against a coming catastrophe no one heeded

history.summary: A war fought partly in the heavens tore open the sky. Whether it was hubris, betrayal, or an outside power, it let the Storm into the world. The Skyward Isles date from here, when land was flung upward and never came down.
events: The breaking of the sky and the descent of the living Storm
The tearing loose of the Skyward Isles
The first Fallen seraphim, who chose the ground over the Heights

history.summary: With the sky broken, the Old Empire shattered. Its capital was lost, its throne sundered, and the united peoples scattered into the survivor-cultures of today.
events: The fall of the imperial capital
The Sundering of the Throne, which no one has since been able to claim
The scattering of the Kin into their homelands

history.summary: The unleashed Storm ravaged the coasts and raised the Stormreach as a permanent tempest-belt. Whole coastal nations drowned; the seaborn say some simply moved below the waves.
events: The permanent storm settling over the Stormreach
The drowning of the coastal kingdoms
The seaborn descent beneath the Sapphire Sea

history.summary: A second lost civilization in the south burned in a single generation, leaving the Ashen Wastes and the Glass Capital. The fire never fully went out.
events: The burning of the southern empire
The fusing of the Glass Capital in one night
The kindling of the Everburn that still burns

history.summary: As light failed at the world's edges, the vampire courts rose and the Shadowlands spread. The Blood Wars were less one war than a century of border-conflicts between the living and the returned that finally ended in uneasy truce.
events: The rise of the night-courts in the Shadowlands
The century of border-wars between the living and the returned
The Dusk Accord that ended open war and drew the shadow-border

history.age: The Shattering of the Old Empire (last echoes)
history.summary: The last imperial successor-states fell, salvage-lords and free cities replaced kings, and the guilds and companies that rule the Crownlands today took power in the vacuum.
events: The fall of the last successor-kingdom
The chartering of the free cities and merchant guilds
The beginning of the salvage-wars over imperial vaults

history.age: The Age of Legends (the present day)
history.summary: The current age. The great empires are gone and the world is wide open. There is no single throne, no single power, and no shortage of ruins, oaths, and vanished cities waiting for someone bold enough to matter. This is the age of adventurers.
events: The opening of the imperial vaults by freelance blades
The waking of things that slept through the fall
The first signs, some say, that the sky may break a second time

factions.name: The Crown Concord
factions.desc: A fractious council of Crownlands duchies and free cities that meets to prevent open war over the vacant imperial throne. It agrees on almost nothing except that no one else should sit the Sundered Throne.
goals: Prevent any single power from claiming the throne

factions.name: The Goldhand League
factions.desc: The banking and trade guild that quietly funds half the Crownlands. It fields no army but owns many, and a Goldhand ledger has toppled more lords than any sword.
goals: Profit from every war without fighting one

factions.name: The Lantern Order
factions.desc: An order of lantern-bearing wardens who seal dangerous imperial vaults and lay imperial dead to rest. They are trusted because they take no side and want no throne.
goals: Seal what the Old Empire buried
Keep dangerous salvage out of ambitious hands

factions.name: The Greycloak Company
factions.desc: The largest free company in the Crownlands, greycloaked sell-swords who fight for whoever pays and remember whoever doesn't. Many adventurers get their start under a grey cloak.
goals: Grow into a power in its own right
Settle old scores from unpaid contracts

factions.name: The Stormwardens
factions.desc: Storm-priests who claim to read and sometimes steer the living Storm. They guard the ridgeline halls and decide, dangerously, when the Storm is angry.
goals: Interpret the will of the Storm
Prevent others from provoking the tempest

factions.name: The Skybell Choir
factions.desc: Keepers of the bronze bells that never stop ringing in the wind. They believe the bells keep the worst of the Storm at bay and that silence means catastrophe.
goals: Warn the holds when a bell falls silent

factions.name: The Gale Riders
factions.desc: Daredevils who ride the wind on gliders and storm-broken mounts, raiding calm harbors and racing the lightning. They think the Stormwardens are cowards.
goals: Free the Storm from those who would cage it

factions.name: The Forgemoot
factions.desc: The council of forge-city masters that sets the price of steel and the law of the peaks. Slow, proud, and unmovable, the Forgemoot has outlasted every empire that tried to command it.
goals: Keep the vaults sealed and the grudges recorded

factions.name: The High Clans
factions.desc: The sky-bridge clans of the high peaks, goliath and their allies, who measure worth by the Crossing of Nine Bridges and answer to no forge-city.
goals: Uphold clan honor and the Crossing
Stay free of the forge-cities' politics

factions.name: The Deep Conclave
factions.desc: The uneasy alliance of Deep peoples who keep the Sunless Market neutral and the surface out. It speaks with one voice only when the deeper dark stirs.

factions.name: The Greenwardens
factions.desc: Guardians of the Emerald Wilds who answer to the Heartwood, not to any crown. They mediate between the forest's many peoples and punish those who cut too deep.
goals: Protect the Heartwood and the old growth
Heal what the loggers and the Hunt wound

factions.name: The Tide Covenant
factions.desc: The seaborn confederation that claims the deep water and levies tolls on surface trade. It sees itself as the sea's rightful government and the free-captains as pirates.
goals: Bring the surface trade to heel

factions.name: The Free Captains
factions.desc: A loose brotherhood of independent ship-captains who refuse the covenant's tolls and keep Port Meridian free. Half smugglers, half heroes, depending on the harbor.
goals: Answer to no crown, above or below the waves

factions.name: The Sky Covenant
factions.desc: The governing pact of the drifting isles, seraphim and birdkin and harengon together, charged with keeping the isles aloft and the chain-bridges open.
goals: Discover what still holds the isles up

factions.name: The Night Court
factions.desc: The ruling vampire houses of the Shadowlands, ancient, patient, and bound by the Dusk Accord. Not all are villains; many simply intend to outlive the problem.

factions.name: The Unlit
factions.desc: A cult, drawn from every Kin, that believes the sun is a wound and means to put it out. The one thing the Night Court and the living agree must be stopped.
goals: Recover anything that can dim a light

factions.name: The Radiant Choir
factions.desc: The seraphim orthodoxy of the Celestial Heights, keepers of star-fire and the oldest prophecies. Rigid, luminous, and increasingly afraid of a prophecy they cannot silence.
goals: Prevent a second breaking of the sky

factions.name: The Marchwardens
factions.desc: The border-guard of the Elemental Marches, sworn to keep the elemental realms from spilling inland and to watch the rifts. They distrust anyone who bargains with the elements.

settlements.name: Highreach
settlements.landmark: The Sundered Throne kept under glass in the old imperial hall
settlements.conflict: Guilds and old nobility struggle for control of the throne-hall and what it symbolizes
rumors: The Throne whispered a name last winter
A Goldhand banker is buying every vault-map in the city
hooks: Guard, or steal, the Sundered Throne
Investigate the whispering in the throne-hall

settlements.name: Bridgewater
settlements.populationType: River port on stilts and bridges, ~40,000
settlements.landmark: The Drowned Palace visible beneath the clear river
settlements.conflict: Salvage crews fight over the right to dive the Drowned Palace
rumors: Lights move in the Drowned Palace at night
A diver came up speaking a dead imperial tongue
hooks: Dive the Drowned Palace
Find out what the diver saw before the guild silences him

settlements.name: Ninebridge Hold
settlements.landmark: The Nine Bridges over a gorge, each a coming-of-age crossing
settlements.conflict: A bridge is failing and the Warden hides it to avoid losing face
rumors: The seventh bridge groans in the wind now
The Warden's heir refused the Crossing
hooks: Repair or re-consecrate a failing bridge
Escort a coward's Crossing

settlements.name: Thundergate
settlements.landmark: The Standing Bolt, frozen lightning above the gate
settlements.conflict: Stormwardens and Gale Riders fight over whether to cage or free the Storm
rumors: The Standing Bolt flickered, which it has never done
A Gale Rider heard the Storm say a name
hooks: Discover why the Standing Bolt is dying
Broker peace, or pick a side, in the storm-cult feud

settlements.name: Skybell Reach
settlements.landmark: Ten thousand bronze bells that ring without pause
settlements.conflict: One great bell has fallen silent and the Choir is terrified of what it means
rumors: The silent bell was the oldest one
Something climbed the bell-tower and did not come down
hooks: Find why the great bell fell silent
Recover a bell-ringer lost in the tower

settlements.name: Durnhal
settlements.landmark: The Everforge, burning since before the Sundering
settlements.conflict: The Everforge is dimming and rival clans blame one another
rumors: The Everforge dims when a certain vault is opened below
A forge-master has gone missing in the deep levels
hooks: Find why the Everforge is failing
Recover a stolen master-rune

settlements.name: Cloudanvil
settlements.landmark: An anvil-shaped peak above the cloud line
settlements.conflict: A vault-claim dispute threatens to become a clan war
rumors: Something is nesting on the anvil-peak
The Crossing has grown deadlier this season
hooks: Mediate the vault-claim before it turns to war
Clear the anvil-peak of its new tenant

settlements.name: Emberdeep
settlements.landmark: The Sealed Door no one has opened and lived
settlements.conflict: Something knocks on the Sealed Door from the far side
rumors: The knocking keeps a rhythm now
A vault-keeper deserted rather than stand another watch
hooks: Stand watch on the Sealed Door
Discover what the knocking is spelling out

settlements.name: Elarethil
settlements.landmark: A city of living trees woven into towers
settlements.conflict: The Thorn Court's isolationism is splitting the city against the Canopy Pact
rumors: The Heartwood is sickening
A Thorn Court noble was found with logger's coin
hooks: Carry a message across the Court's closed borders
Find the source of the Heartwood's sickness

settlements.name: Green Hollow
settlements.landmark: The tree line where farm meets old growth
settlements.conflict: Settlers press the tree line and the beast-kin ranges push back
rumors: The Hunt rode past the town by daylight
A wolfkin range has gone quiet
hooks: Broker a border between settlers and beast-kin
Investigate why the Hunt rides by day

settlements.name: Cinderhold
settlements.landmark: A fortress built into a dormant cinder-cone
settlements.conflict: Ash-clans raid Cinderhold for its rare water-cistern
rumors: The Everburn is spreading toward the hold
An elder heard the fire speak
hooks: Defend the water-cistern from raiders
Escort a pilgrim into the Everburn

settlements.name: Glasswatch
settlements.landmark: Overlook of the fused Glass Capital
settlements.conflict: Everyone wants a guide into the Glass Capital and few guides return
rumors: A vault in the Glass Capital never burned
The ash-wraiths are following salvagers home
hooks: Guide an expedition into the Glass Capital
Recover an unburned relic before a rival crew

settlements.name: Fjordheim
settlements.landmark: The Aurora Vault where dead kings lie under ice
settlements.conflict: A dead king is thawing out of the Aurora Vault
rumors: The aurora has changed color over the vault
The oldest king's tomb is cracked open
hooks: Guard, or investigate, the thawing Aurora Vault
Sail against the ice-reavers

settlements.name: Whitehall
settlements.landmark: A hall carved inside a living glacier
settlements.conflict: The Winter Hunt has crossed south of its old bounds
rumors: The Hunt takes only those who break an oath
A keeper walked into the glacier and never came out
hooks: Turn back or appease the Winter Hunt
Recover a keeper lost in the glacier

settlements.name: The Oasis of Karan
settlements.landmark: The last great spring before the deep dunes
settlements.conflict: The league and the sun-court fight over oasis tariffs
rumors: A storm uncovered a city in the deep dunes
Someone is selling maps to Karan-That-Was
hooks: Escort a caravan to a newly-uncovered ruin
Protect, or steal, the buried-city maps

settlements.name: Sunspire
settlements.landmark: A mile-high needle that casts no shadow at noon
settlements.conflict: The sun-court's heir is lost in the deep dunes
rumors: The Spire's tip has begun to glow at night
The lost heir was seen alive in a mirage
hooks: Search the dunes for the lost heir
Learn why the Spire glows

settlements.name: Duskhollow
settlements.government: The Moon Court (by masks and favors)
settlements.landmark: Silvermere, the lake that shows your fate
settlements.conflict: One of the Nine Lanterns has gone out and the dark is creeping in
rumors: A face in Silvermere wept without a person
A kitsune noble is collecting favors, which never ends well
hooks: Relight the failed Lantern
Repay, or escape, a kitsune's dangerous favor

settlements.name: Silvermere
settlements.landmark: The fate-showing lake it is named for
settlements.conflict: Someone is trafficking stolen dreams and the wardens are hunting them
rumors: A dream-thief sells other people's memories in Duskhollow
The lake showed the same fate to three strangers
hooks: Hunt the dream-thief
Discover why one fate is shared by three

settlements.name: Lowvault
settlements.landmark: The Sunless Market, neutral ground for all Deep peoples
settlements.conflict: Something is coming up through the Deepest Door below the city
rumors: The Deepest Door's wards are cracking
